title: Patch: the skill miss reads only what its seat may know
thread:
**Issue #4216 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4216: Patch: the skill miss reads only what its seat may know
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When you face a ladder bot that is set below full strength, some of its moves come from a deliberate mistake routine instead of the full search. That routine is supposed to play as if it knew only what its seat could see at the table. Today two corners of it peek at the real hidden cards: the list of moves it chooses from is built from the true position rather than the seat's view, and the imaginary worlds it prices those moves on ignore the cost printed on a face-down card that both players can see. After this change the bot's mistakes are honest ones: it picks only from moves its seat could know about, and its imagined worlds respect the costs it was shown. A concrete case: a human with a face-down card showing a cost faces a weaker bot whose error routine currently prices its reply on worlds holding a different-cost card, and whose shortlist of moves can shift with cards it cannot see.

## Why

- The crate's contract is that hidden cards never change a decision (`crates/ai/README.md`, decide reads only through redact; `decide.rs` names ai_to_act and redact the only two reads of the true state under R185). The mistake routine is a decision path used by ladder bots (`BOT_STRENGTHS`) and any seat below full skill, but `skill.rs` builds its candidate list from the true state and determinizes with shown-cost matching switched off, unlike every search-time determinization.
- Face-down cards are not inert while hidden: a face-down trap's aura is live (R403) and visibly moves unit stats (the R602 compensation in `observe.rs`), and a face-down card can show a cost that redaction preserves and determinization matches (R351, R762). Both feed legality and pricing, so a true-state list and a cost-blind world can answer differently from what the seat knows.
- Nothing guards this path today: the quality gates and the shadow-ban sweep always play `skill: None` (`gate.rs`, `sweep.rs`), so only short unit tests exercise the miss. A hidden-information regression here ships to real human opponents silently.

## Proposal

- Derive the miss's candidate list from the redacted state it already computes, instead of the true state.
- Determinize the miss's world with the default shown-cost matching, as the search's worlds do, so its one-ply prices are read on worlds consistent with what the seat was shown; keep it off only with a documented, measured reason and a test.
- Update the crate README's skill paragraph, which currently documents the true-state candidates, and any comments describing the old behavior.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/skill.rs` (candidate source, determinize options)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/skill.rs` (new fairness tests)
- `crates/ai/README.md` (skill paragraph)
- SPEC sections 9.9 (no-cheating practice AI, R185) and 9.12 (skill knob, R747000, R2214000); no new ruling, since this enforces R185 rather than deciding new semantics

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skill_miss_action` builds its candidates from `redact(state, seat)`, never from the true state.
- [ ] Its determinized world respects shown costs (R762) like the search's worlds, or a comment plus a test records why it must not.
- [ ] A new test plays positions whose redactions match but whose hidden cards differ, including a face-down card with a shown cost and one with a live stat aura, and holds the miss's candidates and draw sequence identical; the shown-cost half fails before the fix.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` with the testkit features, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean, and gate and sweep behavior at `skill: None` is unchanged.

## Size and risks

Small: one module plus tests and a paragraph of docs; no engine, card, gate-threshold, or spec change (difficulty hard as AI work goes, priority low as fairness work goes). The risk is that some candidate today is reachable only through hidden info; losing it is the intended fix, and the full-skill AI plus all gates are untouched. If shown-cost matching proves load-bearing for the miss, the fallback keeps it off with a measured reason instead.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44420828174)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`skill_miss_action` (`crates/ai/src/skill.rs`) stops peeking at hidden cards: it lists its candidates from `redact(state, seat)` instead of the true state, and it determinizes its one-ply world with the default shown-cost matching (`DeterminizeOptions::default()`, R762) like the search's worlds do. The crate README's skill paragraph is updated to match, with tests that pin both behaviors.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/ai/src/skill.rs` | change | `skill_miss_action` doc comment (R2214000); `candidate_set(&public, seat)`; `DeterminizeOptions::default()` |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/skill.rs` | change | New `r185_skill_miss_*` guard tests and `r762_skill_miss_*` fail-before tests, plus imports |
| `crates/ai/README.md` | change | Skill paragraph in Matches and the quality gates (true-state candidates → redacted candidates, default sampler) |

Must not touch: `crates/ai/src/gate.rs`, `sweep.rs`, `match_.rs`, `baselines.rs`, `decide.rs`, `determinize.rs`, `observe.rs`, `candidates.rs`, `config.rs`; `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/server`, `apps/`; anything under `spec/` (no new ruling, no `spec/pending/4216.md`, never `cargo jackioh spec index`); `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: §9.9 (R185), §9.12 (R747000, R2214000); background R762, R351, R602/R403. Governing code contract: `crates/ai/README.md` (`decide` reads only `redact`).

## Steps

1. Re-read before editing: `spec/09-architecture.md` §§9.9, 9.12; `spec/rulings/R0185.md`, `R2214000.md`, `R747000.md`, `R0762.md`; all of `crates/ai/src/skill.rs` (95 lines); `decide.rs` step 4 (`probe_world`, `candidate_actions(&probe, …)`), the honest-candidate pattern to mirror.
2. In `crates/ai/src/skill.rs`, replace the `skill_miss_action` doc comment's first two lines (`the true state's candidates (each legal), read one ply ahead on one determinization`) with: the redacted state's candidates (R185: `candidate_set` on `redact(state, seat)`), read one ply ahead on one determinization at the shown costs (`determinize` with the default options, R762). Keep the R2214000 cite and the rest of the comment.
3. In `skill_miss_action`, change line 60 `candidate_set(state, seat)` to `candidate_set(&public, seat)`. Change lines 64–71 `DeterminizeOptions { match_shown_cost: Some(false) }` to `DeterminizeOptions::default()`. No import changes (`DeterminizeOptions` is still named; `state` is still used by `ai_to_act` and `redact`).
4. In `crates/ai/README.md`, in the skill paragraph, replace `over the greedy baseline's one-ply scores of the true state's candidates, read on one determinization of what the seat sees` with `over the greedy baseline's one-ply scores of the redacted state's candidates (R185: only moves the seat could know about), read on one determinization of what the seat sees at the shown costs (R762: the search's default sampler)`.
5. Extend the imports of `crates/ai/tests/ai/skill.rs`: add `candidate_set, action_key, redact, skill_miss_action` to the `jackioh_ai` import; add `GameState, create_rng` to the `testkit` import; extend `use super::support::random_decks;` with `AI, HUMAN, register_cards, scenario`.
6. Add guard test `r185_skill_miss_matches_on_redactions_that_match`: build scenario pair A/B (AI=p1 to act, turn 9, p1 with attackers, a playable hand card and mana, following `siphoned()`'s keys in `redact_live_face_down.rs`) whose hidden cards differ but redactions must match — B swaps p2's hand/library defs for different ones, and a second pair C/D puts face-down `classic-088` Siphon Squad non-Radiant vs Radiant (the aura card; its aura sleeps per R1149000 so shown stats and cost match). Assert the precondition `serde_json::to_value(redact(&a, AI)) == serde_json::to_value(redact(&b, AI))`; assert candidate-set equality as sorted `action_key` vecs, both redacted-vs-redacted and true-vs-redacted; then for 50 seeds `create_rng(&format!("r185-miss:{k}"), 0)` assert `skill_miss_action` returns `Some` and equal actions for A vs B with equal `rng.cursor()` after. This test passes before the fix too — say so in a comment; it guards the candidate source.
7. Add fail-before test `r762_skill_miss_prices_its_reply_on_worlds_at_the_shown_cost`: copy the `shroomed(true)` fixture from `determinize_shown_cost.rs` (face-down `classicplus-001` Doom Shroom showing cost 4; `stinkyscape-022`/`stinkyscape-174` in p2's graveyard so a cost-matched world always holds Doom Shroom, which exiles both attackers). After applying the fix, scan seeds `r762-miss:{k}` for k in 0..500, pick 3 seeds whose post-fix pick is a specific non-attack action, and pin `(seed, action_key)` pairs asserting equality plus `!matches!(action, ActionBody::Attack { .. })`. Verify it fails before the fix by temporarily restoring `match_shown_cost: Some(false)`, running the test, then re-applying the fix.
8. Run: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai skill`, then full `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`. Confirm the pre-existing `r2214000_zero_skill_plays_the_miss_not_the_random_policy` still passes (rejected empty, no fallbacks: every redacted-listed candidate stays true-state legal).

## Tests

- `crates/ai/tests/ai/skill.rs`, `r185_skill_miss_matches_on_redactions_that_match`: equal redactions (hand-swap pair, Siphon radiant-flag pair) give equal candidate sets and equal per-seed miss actions plus equal rng cursors. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-ai skill`.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/skill.rs`, `r762_skill_miss_prices_its_reply_on_worlds_at_the_shown_cost`: pinned seeds on the Doom-Shroom position give the recorded non-attack picks; fails with cost matching off, passes with `DeterminizeOptions::default()`. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-ai skill`.
- Existing `r747000_full_skill_matches_unskilled` and `r2214000_zero_skill_plays_the_miss_not_the_random_policy` in the same file cover skill:None gate/sweep behavior (unchanged files, no draws at full skill, miss moves legal). Full crate: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`.

## Done when

- [ ] `skill_miss_action` builds candidates from `redact(state, seat)`; no true-state read remains in it besides `ai_to_act`/`redact`.
- [ ] Its world uses `DeterminizeOptions::default()` (shown-cost matching on).
- [ ] New R185 guard test and R762 fail-before test pass; the R762 test was seen to fail with matching off.
- [ ] README skill paragraph documents redacted candidates and the default sampler.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check` clean; no spec/ file added or edited.

## Risks

- A candidate reachable only through hidden info would disappear from the miss. That is the intended fix; the true-vs-redacted set-equality assertion plus the unchanged zero-skill match test (no rejected moves, no fallbacks) prove nothing legal was lost on the sampled positions.
- `legal_actions` on the redacted state meets `ai:hidden` placeholders. `decide` step 4 already asserts the seat's own legality never depends on hidden cards; the guard test proves it on the new positions.
- R602's `agrees()` takes no rng draws, so flipping cost matching changes world contents, not draw counts; the cursor-equality assertion pins the draw sequence.
- Softmax picks are probabilistic, so the R762 test pins exact seeded `(seed, action_key)` pairs instead of asserting frequencies — deterministic, not flaky.

## Open questions

- R2214000's ("lists the seat's candidates on the true state") and R747000's ("the miss takes only its legal list from the true state") sentences go stale under this fix. Amending a ruling note needs its own ruling, and the task orders no spec change, so the builder leaves `spec/` alone; a person should file a follow-up to amend the prose. Nothing else needs a person: no new ruling, no migration, no dashboard or secret.
```
